items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: I used to have a four-piece band there. And I had lucky enough to have three New Orleans men in four in the band. We had four pieces. Like Thomas Taylor, he was on drums.

ctx.x: Do you remember if there was much jazz on the riverboats at those times, or was it earlier?

You mean here or in Chicago? Well, both here and in Chicago. Well, I used to play on a boat in Chicago at the Navy Pier. That's a recreation pier that extends about a mile, I think, out in Lake Michigan. I used to play on a little excursion boat that makes trips from the pier for a half hour. I used to have a four-piece band there. And I had lucky enough to have three New Orleans men in four in the band. We had four pieces. Like Thomas Taylor, he was on drums. And Alcorn, this Alcorn boy, he was on tenor sax. And…
Did you notice, did many white Chicago musicians take any notice of the New Orleans musicians, all that style at that time, and try to emulate it?
